title.narrative: Restore access to critical health services to Cuban local communities in post-Hurricane Rafael aftermath

description.narrative: Hurricane Rafael made landfall in western Cuba as a Category 3 hurricane, on the afternoon of 6 November 2024. The province of Artemisa reported the greatest damage, across 11 municipalities. 192 health institutions have reported damage affecting their service delivery capacity and/or safety of operating conditions, of which 62% belong to Artemisa. Artemisa province is reporting the most damage to health infrastructure with 119 health institutions affected, including 4 hospitals and16 polyclinics among others. Mayabeque reported 17 health facilities with damage, and Havana reported damage to 12 hospitals and 7 polyclinics. These impacts to health services are occurring in the context of a complex epidemiological situation, with co-circulation of dengue, Oropouche and various respiratory viruses, added to the current context of energy crisis in the country. The inability of the health system to respond promptly and efficiently enough to deal with disease outbreaks is concerning as it may accentuate the risks of spread of infectious diseases faced by the affected populations.This CERF project will support the rapid recovery of the operational capacity of at least 87 affected health institutions in the two (2) most impacted provinces (Artemisa and Mayabeque) and support the timely detection and control/management of health risks and arising health threats faced by vulnerable populations living in affected areas, including mental health affectation as well as risks of communicable disease outbreaks. Funds will be used to procure and deliver essential relief items as well as medicines and medical supplies and equipment to affected health institutions to restore operations and support continued care delivery capacity to people living in affected municipalities. The project will target the recuperation of operating conditions and continuity of care delivery in all affected hospitals and polyclinics and at least 50% of the affected smaller health posts in the two targeted provinces. PAHO/WHO will also support the intensification of epidemiological surveillance and water quality monitoring activities to ensure the timely detection of disease outbreaks, particularly of water-borne and vector-borne diseases in the current context of deteriorated WASH conditions as well as active circulation of infectious pathogens. Activities will focus on the procurement of supplies and equipment, as well as rapid training of health personnel. These interventions will help ensure continued access to quality essential health services to over 395,000 individuals living in the most affected communities by Hurricane Rafael.
